title: The catalytic cycle of NQO1 wildtype
author: Anoz Carbonell, Ernesto
license_note: Zenodo record metadata license field: cc-by-4.0

steps.title: Prepare anaerobic buffer
steps.instruction: Make 20 mM HEPES‑KOH, pH 7.4, degas or purge with inert gas to ensure anaerobic conditions.

steps.title: Prepare NQO1 holo solution
steps.instruction: Dilute purified NQO1 holo protein to a final concentration of 7.5 µM in the anaerobic buffer.

steps.title: Prepare coenzyme solutions
steps.instruction: Make separate anaerobic solutions of NADH (7.5 µM to 100 µM series), NADPH (7.5 µM), and 4R‑2H‑NADH (NADD, 7.5 µM) in the same buffer.

steps.title: Set up stopped‑flow instrument
steps.instruction: Configure the Applied Photophysics SX.18MV stopped‑flow spectrophotometer with a photodiode‑array detector, verify anaerobic operation, and load the ProData‑SX software for data acquisition.

steps.title: Measure reductive half‑reaction
steps.instruction: Load syringe A with NQO1 holo (7.5 µM) and syringe B with the chosen coenzyme (NADH, NADPH, or NADD) at the desired concentration; mix rapidly in the stopped‑flow cell and record multi‑wavelength absorption from 400 nm to 900 nm.

steps.title: Measure oxidative half‑reaction
steps.instruction: First generate NQO1 hq by mixing NQO1 holo (7.5 µM) with stoichiometric NADH (7.5 µM) under anaerobic conditions; then load syringe A with this NQO1 hq (7.5 µM) and syringe B with 2,6‑Dichlorophenolindophenol (DCPIP, 7.5 µM) and record the same wavelength range.

steps.title: Process kinetic data
steps.instruction: Import the stopped‑flow traces into ProData‑SX, then perform global spectral deconvolution with Pro‑Kineticist using sequential irreversible models (A→B→C or A→B→C→D) to obtain observed rate constants (kobs) and spectra of each species.

steps.title: Determine kinetic isotope effects
steps.instruction: Prepare equimolar mixtures of NQO1 holo (7.5 µM) with NADH or with NADD (7.5 µM); repeat the reductive half‑reaction at several temperatures; calculate KIE as kobs(NADH)/kobs(NADD) for each temperature.

steps.title: Calculate activation parameters
steps.instruction: Plot ln(kobs) versus 1/T for each reaction, fit to the Arrhenius equation, and extract the frequency factor (A) and activation energy (Ea) as described in the referenced protocol.
